959.by: Andrew Beling (ajbeling), research by AI agents
959.supersedes: The 29 October 2026 partly_read review used Green's calendar. With the original unseen, it took the five printed numbers and asterisks for the extent of the unread material. The recto has a short graphic passage and two sustained blocks omitted in print. This revises the verdict for the cipher passages. Green already gives the surrounding English.

seen.where: The National Archives, SP 15/31 f. 63r–v. Gale State Papers Online MC4304880878, scan 65 right (text), 66 left (address); 66 right begins the separate f. 64r letter. https://link.gale.com/apps/doc/MC4304880878/SPOL
seen.extent: One written recto, with cipher signs in the opening and two long blocks. Two independent sign readings of 17 rows in those blocks agree at 445 of 707 aligned candidate positions. The short opening and numbers embedded in the clear prose are additional. These are provisional sign positions, not words or a deciphered fraction.
seen.cipher: The recto mixes clear English, figures and densely written graphic and letter-like signs. The long blocks have no interlinear decipherment. The verso address is to the English cardinal in Rome. The deciphered writing facing it on f. 64r belongs to the following letter.

prior_art.decode: Live DECODE keyword searches for SP 15/31 and William Allen returned zero record rows. Charles Paget returned R3853, R3861, R3871, R3890 and R3898, all State Papers Scotland items of 1585–86. Paget alone also returned R3874, R3886 and R3902. The record notes identify deciphered Mary correspondence, copies and connected papers. See README for references. None names the Brussels–Rome letter. The National Archives returned 28 pages across institutions. Keyword negatives have limited reach.
prior_art.tomokiyo: Cryptiana's Mary Stuart survey identifies a Charles Paget–Mary key (SP 53/22 f. 47) used on three independently dated letters, and a separate Lord Paget key (f. 46). The Elizabethan survey's w.209 denotes Charles Paget in Neville–Cecil correspondence beginning in 1599. Neither survey supplies an Allen reading. https://cryptiana.web.fc2.com/code/mary.htm and https://cryptiana.web.fc2.com/code/elizabeth.htm
prior_art.lasry: Searched Lasry’s published GL index for Paget, Allen, SP 15/31 and 1589. Its Paget? is Clairambault 1225, Genoa 1714. Its 1589 examples concern other correspondents. Lasry, Biermann and Tomokiyo's 2023 Cryptologia article on Mary Stuart's letters concerns 1578–84. https://cryptiana.web.fc2.com/code/GL.htm and https://doi.org/10.1080/01611194.2022.2160677
prior_art.edition: Mary Anne Everett Green, Calendar of State Papers, Domestic Series, Elizabeth and James I, Addenda, 1580–1625 (1872), pp. 279–280, no. 43, prints the clear sense, asterisks and five unresolved numbers. No. 44 is to Barnes and supplies the Parma report. Knox, Letters and Memorials of William Cardinal Allen, pp. 315–316, prints Allen to Lord Paget, 30 January 1590, referring to Charles's alphabet in a different letter. https://archive.org/details/cu31924091775373/page/n292 and https://archive.org/details/lettersmemorials00alle/page/n445
prior_art.literature: Internet Archive full-text search located Green and references to other papers in SP 15/31 in Stephen Alford's The Watchers. HistoCrypt's proceedings search for Paget returned no results. The first eight Cryptologia and first ten general Crossref bibliographic results for the named parties and cipher yielded no edition of the 1589 passages. These are bounded searches of metadata or indexed text.

959.key_check: On fourteen reserved rows (579 candidate positions), the sampled alphabet inventories of old nos. 96, 97 and 97a covered 73, 83 and 52 positions, respectively, with 8, 6 and 3 adjacent pairs. All missed the registered minimum. Of 1,000 shuffled assignments for each, 116, 136 and 465 scored at least as well. These tests supply no deciphered word and cannot exclude related or differently marked systems. The fuller Chartley sheet provided 31 further word and name specimens. Two blind matchers agreed on one hash-like sign at 14 positions, with zero adjacent matched pairs. No word was validated. A positive control applying the short 97a panel to SP 53/15 f. 6r, a 1585 Paget letter for which the fuller Chartley key is identified, also missed: 8 of 109 agreed slots with no adjacency. The September misses cannot exclude a related cipher. A separate January row checked against the fuller Chartley table passed: 86 usable positions out of 110, 69 adjacent pairs, and 49 reference characters against a maximum of 15 in 1,000 shuffles. In a fresh direct comparison on the fourth row of the lower September block, both readers agreed on usable historical values at 22 of 57 positions, with 9 adjacent pairs. The English prediction score was equalled or exceeded by 10 of 1,000 shuffled tables. All three relevant thresholds were missed. The September graphic cipher remains unread.
959.key_held: TNA SP 106/2 ff. 59r, 61r and 62r (old nos. 96, 97 and 97a) were inspected. No. 96 has C.P., no. 97 the Naurys and Remisey aliases, no. 97a Charles Paget and the Queen of Scots. None names Allen. Tomokiyo assigns a further cited witness, SP 53/22 f. 47, to Charles Paget and Mary in 1585–86. We inspected f. 47r and its endorsement on f. 47v. Paired alternatives for H and I and the signs for to and but match old 97a. The Chartley sheet adds word signs, countries, royals, nulls and a doubling mark. No use in the Allen letter is established. https://link.gale.com/apps/doc/MC4322680002/SPOL https://link.gale.com/apps/doc/MC4323480003/SPOL
959.key_in_volume: The same volume contains glossed ciphertext in the next letter, f. 64r (Green no. 44, recipient Barnes), and in Paget's May 1589 instructions to B[arnes], f. 33r (Green no. 27). Two readers compared four complete graphic specimens from f. 64r and two from f. 33r with all 17 long-block rows on f. 63r. Neither accepted an exact occurrence. Both witnesses have independently readable source passages. Neither gives a demonstrable reading on f. 63r. https://link.gale.com/apps/doc/MC4304880841/SPOL
959.duplicates: Repository known.py on SP 15/31, SP15/31, MC4304880878, Charles Paget and Cardinal Allen found the original sweep row and lead 959. Catalogue no. 1009 is to Throgmorton in 1595. Its correspondent and date differ. Public DECODE records in the README concern earlier Mary correspondence. searches.query: DECODE RecordsList: SP 15/31; Charles Paget; William Allen; The National Archives; Paget; Paget's Cipher; SP53-22
searches.result: Five exact-name hits and three additional surname matches described in README. The Paget’s Cipher phrase returns four ciphertext records. The piece search lists key leaves using dual numbering. No Allen text identified.

searches.query: Internet Archive full text: "SP 15/31" decipher; "Charles Paget" "Cardinal Allen" cipher
searches.result: The shelfmark query returned two copies of Alford's The Watchers. The snippets cite Barnes's May questionnaire and several other papers, including a different decipher. The names query returned 864 hits; the first 20 were inspected as search results.

searches.query: Internet Archive full text: "Your letters would come with more speed and safety"
searches.result: All four hits are copies/catalogue versions of Green's calendar. The actual calendar pages print the neighboring English and numbers, with starred omissions in no. 43.

searches.query: HistoCrypt proceedings search Paget; Crossref Cryptologia Charles Paget Cardinal Allen cipher 1589; all-journal bibliographic search Charles Paget William Allen decipher Brussels September 1589
searches.result: No HistoCrypt results; no reading of this text among the first 8 journal records and first 10 all-journal records. Crossref covers registered publication metadata, not every work or its full text.

searches.query: Cryptiana GL.htm: Paget, Allen, SP 15/31, 1589; Mary Stuart survey: Charles Paget and SP 53/22 f. 47
searches.result: The GL Paget hit is dated 1714. The Mary survey supplies a working key for three 1585 letters to Mary and distinguishes the key for Lord Paget on the preceding sheet.

lead_updates.folio_note: Text f. 63r; address f. 63v. Green (1872), Domestic Addenda, no. 43, pp. 279–280.
lead_updates.status: Partly in cipher. The original contains an opening cipher passage and two sustained graphic blocks. Green printed the clear text and five unresolved numbers. No reading of the graphic passages located.
lead_updates.why: Extensive surviving cipher in a dated letter from Charles Paget to Cardinal Allen at Rome, with independently deciphered contemporary Paget material available for comparison.
lead_updates.verify: Confirm disputed sign boundaries against a fresh reading of f. 63r and compare independently dated Paget specimens. Keep the five printed numbers separate from the graphic-block inventory.
lead_updates.access_note: Original in Gale State Papers Online (institutional subscription), MC4304880878, scans 65–66. Public access to Green's printed calendar.

links.label: Green, p. 280, no. 43 ends and no. 44 begins

lead_updates.score_note: The October 2026 importance score came from Green’s printed calendar. The November 19 manuscript review inspected the original and counted two long graphic blocks plus a separate opening. The earlier numerical importance score is retained.
lead_updates.prior_art: Green printed the surrounding English and five numbers. On 19 November 2026 the manuscript, DECODE, Cryptiana, Lasry’s index and other printed and repository sources were checked. Related Paget–Mary letters have period decipherments; no decipherment of these Paget–Allen passages was found. See the dated vetting and its limits.
